title: Boating the Illinois River
seo_title: Boating the Illinois River | Ottawa, IL
seo_description: Boating the Illinois River through Starved Rock Country: uncrowded water, scenic bluffs, free Ottawa docks and easy conditions near Heritage Harbor, Ottawa, IL.
body_html:
Boating on the Illinois River is one of the Midwest's best kept boating secrets. It is far less crowded than most lakes, particularly in northern Illinois, and the scenery is fantastic.

Scenery in the Heart of Starved Rock Country

Flowing through the heart of Starved Rock Country, the river is the best way to see natural areas including Starved Rock and Buffalo Rock State Parks and the bluffs that line the shore.

Plenty of Room to Boat

Quest Express members can boat the entire length of the "Ottawa Pool," which runs from Marseilles Lock to Starved Rock Lock. There is no going around in circles like on many lakes.

  • Dock free of charge at downtown Ottawa, with numerous restaurants and other activities.
  • Anchor and socialize at spots like "Bob's Beach."
  • Explore the islands along the river and the side channels they create.

Easy, Comfortable Boating

Members' favorite aspect of river boating is how easy it is. Even on a windy day with other boat traffic, the waves are rarely very high. Boating is almost always more comfortable than on a big lake, and activities like tubing and skiing are possible just about any time. There is no need to get up early to beat the traffic or wait until the middle of the week to have your fun.
